newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish telecom firm TPSA gets PLN 200 mln loan.
newsitem.headline: Polish telecom firm TPSA gets PLN 200 mln loan.

text.p: A consortium of Polish banks, led by Pekao SA, on Wednesday signed an agreement with the state-owned telecom company TPSA on granting it a 200 million zloty loan for expanding a telephone network, TPSA said.
TPSA said in a statement that the loan would help finance its $1 billion investment plan in 1996. Nearly $600 million of this sum will come from the company's own funds, it said.

It said TPSA planned to invest about $1 billion annually in the next few years to set up about one million new telephone connections per year. TPSA will need more loans for the investment programme, it added.
Apart from the state-owned Pekao SA, the banking consortium comprises eight banks, including Bank Gdanski and PBR SA.
TPSA, slated for a partial sell-off in the next two years, had revenues of 5.4 billion zlotys last year, of which it invested 2.1 billion zlotys, and netted 933 million zlotys.
